title: Augsburg 2-2 Bayern Munich: Neuer's blushes spared by late Brown equaliser
subtitle: Manuel Neuer had a day to forget as Bayern Munich could only draw with Augsburg, with Nathaniel Brown coming to the rescue late on.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich twice came from behind to preserve their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season as Manuel Neuer's errors proved costly in a 2-2 draw against Augsburg.
Robin Fellhauer scored the Bundesliga's fastest-ever goal following a mistake from Neuer, though Ismael Saibari hauled the champions back level in the 55th minute on Saturday.
Augsburg hit back when another blunder from Neuer handed Rodrigo Ribeiro a simple finish, but Nathaniel Brown came off the bench to score the leveller in the 80th minute.

No sooner had Bayern got things underway at WWK Arena, they found themselves behind. Neuer aimed to recover from his loose touch with an attempted chip, only for Fellhauer to steal possession and roll the ball home after just eight seconds.
Augsburg should have doubled their lead in the 35th minute when a corner made it to Chrislain Matsima, but he skewed his effort behind from two yards out.

Harry Kane then turned Aleksandar Pavlovic's teasing cross onto the woodwork in the final action of the first half, and Bayern thought they had got themselves level six minutes after the restart when Luis Diaz acrobatically volleyed Saibari's cross into the net.
But Finn Dahmen, who saw Diaz's effort squirm under his grasp, had his blushes spared after the goal was ruled out for an offside earlier in the build-up.
However, the visitors did find their equaliser soon after, with Saibari sweeping into the bottom-left corner from Kane's pass.
Yet Augsburg regained their lead nine minutes later through Ribeiro, who finished from close range after Neuer failed to deal with Calvin Brackelmann's shot from range.

Bayern were then denied a second twice by the assistant's flag. First, Serge Gnabry tucked home Kane's cross, though the England captain had strayed just beyond the Augsburg defence, before Diaz had a second goal chalked off after Alphonso Davies collected possession in an offside position.
But Vincent Kompany's team restored parity for a second time when Kane's centre was turned in by Brown, and Bayern had their chances to snatch all three points.
Gnabry had the best of them, seeing a goal disallowed and also hitting the post.
Neuer's landmark day soured by errors

Ahead of kick-off, Bayern knew they had the chance to leapfrog Borussia Dortmund and go top of the Bundesliga after Niko Kovac's side drew 2-2 with Werder Bremen on Friday, but they were unusually wasteful and were undone at the back by Neuer's mistakes.

Neuer, at 40 years and 197 days old, overtook Jens Lehmann to become the seventh-oldest player in Bundesliga history, though it will be interesting to see whether Kompany sticks with the veteran goalkeeper or chooses to bring in Jonas Urbig.

Bayern thought they had won it late on when Gnabry finished off the crossbar from a tight angle, but once again, the offside flag was up on the far side, with the decision confirmed after a lengthy VAR review.

The reigning champions finished with a mammoth expected goals (xG) total of 5.02 from their 29 shots, 10 of which were on target, compared to Augsburg's 2.37 from their 12 attempts, with Kane generating the highest individual tally, with 1.55 xG from his eight efforts.
With 11 points from their first five matches, Bayern have made their worst start to a Bundesliga campaign in terms of points since 2010-11 (eight).
